items.title: Hackers Hijack Microsoft 365 Accounts at 79 Organizations Using Stolen Login Tokens
items.description: Hackers compromised Microsoft 365 accounts at 79 organizations by reusing stolen login tokens, recording at least 497 successful sign-ins between July 14 and September 22, 2026. The ten-week campaign also generated more than 200,000 failed login attempts across monitored customer environments. The attackers targeted authenticated sessions rather than relying on password guessing. Similar to…

items.title: Attackers Hijack Dahua IP Cameras in Ukraine Using P2P Access and Auth Weaknesses
items.description: The Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) has issued an alert warning of unauthorized remote access to video surveillance systems manufactured by Dahua. "Cases of compromising IP cameras and DVRs with access to the video stream, changing the device configuration and creating third-party accounts have been recorded," the State Special Communications Service of Ukraine (SSSCIP)

items.title: Hackers Use AI Agents to Target Over 2,250 Microsoft 365 Tenants Through ConnectWise
items.description: Hackers used AI agents and stolen ConnectWise application credentials to attempt access to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, according to Microsoft’s technical investigation report. Microsoft attributed the campaign to Storm-0940, a China-state-aligned group, and said its ARTEX framework accelerated reconnaissance, authentication attempts, and cloud persistence. items.title: OpenAI Codex Breaks USB Encryption in Minutes, Exposing Hardcoded Keys and Security Flaws
items.description: OpenAI Codex helped researcher Xusheng Li uncover flaws in four USB protection products, including hardcoded encryption keys and hidden accounts that allowed files to be decrypted without the owner’s password. In one test, Codex identified the main weakness in seven minutes. The findings expose failures in how these products handle secrets, rather than a breakthrough […] The post OpenAI Codex…

items.title: Researcher Gains Root Access to Samsung Smart TV, Uncovers Extensive User Tracking
items.description: A cybersecurity researcher says he gained root access to a 2025 Samsung Smart TV and found software built to track far more than the picture on the screen. Known online as log4j, he started after the set kept showing ads that seemed oddly specific to his household. items.title: Hackers Abuse Claude’s Official Website and Google Ads to Spread Malware
items.description: Cybercriminals found a simple way to make a fake download page look trustworthy. Instead of registering a lookalike domain, they placed their lure on claude.ai, the official website of Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI assistant. The fake page carried Claude branding and offered what looked like easy steps to install a desktop app. […] The post Hackers Abuse Claude’s Official Website…

items.title: CISA Confirms Active Exploitation of Two PHP2Shell Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
items.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday confirmed active exploitation of the recently patched PHP2Shell flaws by adding them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The PHP vulnerabilities, both rated 9.2 on the CVSS scoring system, facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution on affected deployments - CVE-2026-109618 - An out-of-memory

items.title: Cybersecurity Issue Forces a Major New Mexico Hospital to Divert Patients and Close Clinics
items.description: The University of New Mexico Health System told people not to show up at its main hospital in Albuquerque and canceled appointments at more than 30 clinics. The post Cybersecurity Issue Forces a Major New Mexico Hospital to Divert Patients and Close Clinics appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Hackers Use VLC Media Player and VMware Tools to Load Malware Through DLL Side-Loading
items.description: Hackers are using legitimate VLC Media Player and VMware components to load malware onto Windows systems, hiding harmful code behind familiar software. The activity forms part of three malware campaigns targeting users in Brazil and Portugal through fake legal notices, financial documents, and invoice download pages. The attacks combine phishing, hidden scripts, and trusted programs […] The post…

items.title: So Many AI Security Benchmarks, But None Tell the Whole Story
items.description: Measuring AI model security gets complex fast — a growing patchwork of benchmarks targets different variables in the equation, but none replace testing against your own code and workflows.
